classification.difficultyReason: Apply the exterior angle theorem in varied orientations; part e first requires the equal base angles of an isosceles triangle.

content.prompt: Calculate the value of the pronumeral. You do not need to show reasoning.

spec.description: Long narrow triangle with a right-angle marker at upper left and lower side extended to the right.
spec.mathematics: Interior angles 70° and 90°; exterior a° above the right extension.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens, right-angle marker and unknown only.

spec.description: Rotated triangle with left-to-upper-right side extended beyond the upper-right vertex.
spec.mathematics: Interior 80° at left, 70° at bottom; exterior a° to the right of upper-right vertex.

spec.description: Triangle with right side extended above its apex.
spec.mathematics: 50° at lower left, a° at lower right, exterior 130° to the left of the apex extension.

spec.description: Triangle with its right-to-apex side extended upwards to the left.
spec.mathematics: Interior a° at lower left, 60° at lower right; exterior 110° at apex.

spec.description: Triangle with matching double ticks on its left and upper sides; upper side extended beyond upper right.
spec.mathematics: 100° between the equal sides; exterior a° below the upper-right extension.
spec.answerVisibility: 100°, both equality marks and a° only; inferred base angles are withheld.

answer.worked:
The marked sides are equal, so the two base angles are equal. Let each be $b$.
$$\begin{align*}2b+100^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\b&=40^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle theorem:
$$\begin{align*}a&=100^{\circ}+40^{\circ}\\a&=140^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle with both sides through its lower-left vertex extended beyond that vertex.
spec.mathematics: Interior a° at upper left and 60° at right. Exterior 115° is between the downward left-side extension and the ray towards the right vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and unknown only; both extensions retained.
